regexEscapingGotcha: COST A RESTORE TWICE on 2026-08-26: generating regex source through nested shell + Python quoting double-escapes it. `\\\\b` became a literal backslash in a RegExp constructor; `\\\\d` inside a regex LITERAL produced an unterminated group and broke module load. replacementRule: NEW STANDING METHOD 2026-08-26, learned the hard way. When a change makes the pipeline read a DIFFERENT SOURCE DOCUMENT for an existing record, gains/losses counters are blind to it: the first rescue cut replaced 73 stored menus (45 with an older plan year) and the CONFIDENCE DIFF showed ONE loss, because confident->confident is not a state change. The old break was a VERB-AND-SPELLING LIST and missed Verizon by one word ('equivalent to' vs 'equal to'), Thetford by 'contributes', Ferroglobe by a missing 'contributions' - same shape as v76's FEIN guard. New break matches on SHAPE: a continuation stating its OWN complete head with a different rate or bound does not chain; a restatement of the same head still does. 7 change, 7 byte-identical, 1,265 cached filings -> 2 field diffs, 0 quotes suppressed.
gateMatchArm: parser-gate.mjs now asserts MATCH labels too (expect.match), not just vesting. Two v91 specimens pin both directions: 20251014104315NAL0001234147001 must be single-tier (union tiers must not chain), 20251219112023NAL0003370419001 must keep both tiers (same-population continuation). A guard wide enough to fix the first will silently eat the second, so neither ships alone.
auditBlindSpot: The formula-vs-quote correctness check only asks whether the label's NUMBERS appear in its own quote. It cannot see a label assembled from two different sentences about two different populations. That is why the splice class needed hand reading, and why 'the audit is green' is not evidence a label is true.
verifyAgainstTheDocument: STANDING METHOD, learned 2026-08-26 the expensive way. v91 was verified against STORED QUOTES (300-char, whitespace-normalized) and passed; production still shipped the splice. A quote is the extractor's own output, so testing against it verifies the extractor against itself. Verify a parser change against the REAL filing text (pdftotext -layout of the actual PDF). This is also why entries now record fbAck: the investigation needed the prior-year document and had no way to name it.
rescueProvenanceRules: The withdrawn-filing rescue obeys two rules that took three runs to get right. (1) GAP-FILL: content from the plan's OWN newest filing is never replaced by a prior-year read. (2) REFRESHABLE: content the rescue itself wrote (fb for the schedule, featFb for the notes) MAY be re-read by a newer parser - without this a rescued entry freezes forever, since the withdrawn filing can never be downloaded again. The protection keys on PROVENANCE, never on presence. Corollary caught in run #180: protected notes win even when the fallback also has notes (26 plans had newest-filing notes overwritten, one displaying a superseded formula).
ocrChurn: Rescue-written entries can churn slightly when re-read: OCR is not deterministic across runs (the Actions cache is keyed per shard, and shard assignment changes with the shard count, so a re-read may re-rasterize). Measured in run #181: 20 fb-sourced menus differed - one gained 11 funds, one changed a single row name, the rest differed only in values. Expect small churn on this class; it is not a regression signal by itself.
vestingCandidate: NOTED, not started (2026-08-27): Verizon Management's 2024 filing states 'shall be fully vested in the employer-matching and profit sharing contributions ... upon completing three years of vesting service' and the extractor returns quote-only. The Northrop specimen proves 'upon completion of three years' DOES extract, so 'upon completing' may be one word outside the pattern. SIZE THE CLASS FIRST - the standing predicate rule applies, and two gate specimens deliberately assert silence for nearby shapes ('Upon three years of service', 'do not vest ... until after three years').
precedenceRule: STANDING METHOD 2026-08-28. A NEW extraction pass enters at the BOTTOM of the precedence order and is promoted only with evidence. v92 broke the sentence loop and preempted the filed TABLE readers, so 48 plans lost a real six-step schedule to one money type's sentence; v93 fixed that and then preempted the 4-6 year horizon fallback, so 19 plans lost their full-vesting horizon the same way. Both times the new reader was right about the sentence and wrong about its rank. Corollary: a label that CHANGES SHAPE is a change even when the coverage totals do not move, because Graded-to-cliff is invisible to a count - diff the labels, not the totals.
immediateArbitrationDeferred: OPEN, evidenced, do not start without sizing it. v92 produced 157 Immediate-to-cliff flips; most are correct (the plan vests deferrals immediately and employer money over years) but the class is not separable by any rule tried. Counterexamples run both ways: United states a plan-wide three-year cliff AND a bullet where pre-merger flight attendants are always fully vested, so the cliff is the rule; another plan vests matching immediately and non-matching over three years, where no single label is complete. Needs a money-type arbitration pass with its own evidence. Full detail in docs/accuracy-log.md, 2026-08-28.
vestingNow: 51,679 of 68,166 full-form filers (75.8%) after v94, up from 50,987 at v91. Quote-only pool 5,162. The 1,628-row floor whose filings state no number at all is unchanged and unreachable by extraction.
